sentences.text: Days with an air temperature high of 90°F or more averaged 1.3 days a year in the 2000s, and 2.2 days a year over 2016 to 2025, the last 10 years.
The trend test found no clear trend yet, so the record does not point in either direction.
Climate models project about +4.8 more days a year at or above 90°F by 2041 to 2050, and the models disagree, with changes from +2.0 to +6.8 days a year.
These projections are for a typical year in 2041 to 2050, on climate-model grids of about 20–50 km, downscaled by Open-Meteo to about 10 km, and are not a forecast of any single year.
The models follow a high-emissions path and run hotter than the record here, so only their change is shown, and a no clear trend result means 26 years are too few or too variable to tell.

past-air-hot-days.title: Days with an air temperature high of 90°F or more
past-air-hot-days.origin: Open-Meteo historical weather archive (ERA5 reanalysis), daily, 2000 to 2025. Counted from the daily record at this address.
past-air-hot-days.text: Days with an air temperature high of 90°F or more, 2000 to 2025. 2000s: 1.3 days a year on average (13 days in 10 years); 2016 to 2025 (the last 10 years): 2.2 days a year on average (22 days in 10 years). Trend test (Mann-Kendall with Sen slope, one value per year; a trend counts only if p is under 0.05). Result: no clear trend yet.

future-hot-days.title: Days per year with an air-temperature high of 90°F or more, in climate models
future-hot-days.origin: Open-Meteo Climate API (CMIP6 HighResMIP models), daily temperature_2m_max. 7 of 7 CMIP6 HighResMIP models had data for this point.
future-hot-days.text: The climate models' own change in days a year at or above 90°F (air temperature, not feels-like), 7 models. Climate models: 4.1/yr (2001 to 2020, models) to 8.9/yr (2041 to 2050), about +4.8 days a year. Across models the change ranges from +2.0 to +6.8 days a year. Models range from 1.8 to 9.4 in 2001 to 2020 and from 3.8 to 12.1 in 2041 to 2050. These models run hotter than the weather record counted at this spot, so the change is shown, not their raw level.

caveat.title: What the projections are, and are not
caveat.origin: Open-Meteo Climate API; CMIP6 HighResMIP climate models
caveat.text: Climate models (CMIP6) are physics simulations, not a forecast; they run hotter than the record here, so we show their change. These models follow a high-emissions path (as close to RCP8.5 as CMIP6 gets). We show how much they say it changes, not their raw level. The models run on climate-model grids of about 20–50 km, downscaled by Open-Meteo to about 10 km, and they disagree, so the range across models is shown. They describe how often hot days could occur in a typical year of 2041 to 2050, not what any single year or day will do. A trend in the past record is reported only when a statistical test gives p under 0.05; otherwise the record says "no clear trend yet", which means the 26 years are too few or too variable to tell.
